adjacent-overload-signatures.reason: PASS, genuine. Port matches getMisplacedOverloads: the member's key (name normalised over identifier, string, number and literal computed names; computed expressions by text; static-ness; call and construct signatures by kind) is bound and must appear on an earlier sibling, while the previous member must not share it. 'Previous member' is a recursive util that skips any run of `;`, `,` and comments (and accessors under ignore-accessors) between members, and comments between statements (an empty statement resets the key, as in TSLint). Numeric names compare by source text (TSLint normalises `0x10` to `16`). End positions differ where tree-sitter leaves a member's trailing `;` outside the node.

evidence.why: `"a"();` shares key `a` with the identifier `a()` two members earlier: the string_fragment binding compares equal to the property_identifier by text

no-switch-case-fall-through.reason: Since M3, tsutils' endsControlFlow (no checker, as the walker calls it) is recursive utils: jumps; blocks and clauses where any reached statement ends; if/else with both branches ending (constant true/false conditions pick one); while(true)/for(;;)/do whose body ends with no unlabeled break or continue collected from it; switch with a default whose last clause ends and no collected unlabeled break; try/catch/finally. A statement is collected only if no earlier sibling ends control flow, and nested loops/switches filter their own jumps. One approximation: a labeled statement is treated as not ending if it contains any labeled break/continue (TSLint compares the label). Findings anchor at the `case`/`default` keyword.

evidence.why: `case 2:` follows outer `case 1:` whose nested switch always returns (default clause ends, no collected break), so no FP
